who_qualified: aged 15–35 (ads shown to 18–35); reached the end of the questions, about 21 minutes in
qualify_rule: answered the last question before the contact and payment questions
notes: Pilot of the next recruitment's survey: gender x inside/outside 81 radius areas around towns. The ad message offered 260 KES of airtime until 25 Sep 2024 and 130 KES after. Insights recorded no impressions field for these runs; impressions are spend / CPM (CPM $1.9-2.5, a USD account). Cost per person who started is very low ($0.04) and matches Meta's own count of conversations started (see private map). qualify_point counts every prompt answered, including 'OK' taps.

who_qualified: aged 15–35 (ads shown to 18–35), answered the gender question as a woman or a man; reached the end of the questions, about 19 minutes in
qualify_rule: answered the last question before the contact and payment questions
notes: Same survey and radius areas as KE-2024-09. Ads ran 5-7 Feb 2025 to women and men, then from 11 Feb to women only (renamed ad sets). People carry only the inside/outside label, so the 5-7 Feb cells pool the men's and women's ad sets. People already counted in KE-2024-09 are not counted again. Impressions are spend / CPM (no impressions field recorded).

who_qualified: aged 18–24 by the ads, mostly women, chosen by Meta interests; gave a phone number and reached the end of the questions, about 13 minutes in
qualify_rule: answered the final phone-number question (the payment step)
notes: Five audience groups, each an ad set with its own ages (18, 18-21, 22-24), gender and Meta interests/behaviours; followers of the sponsor's pages excluded. Two groups excluded cities: 10 cities at 16 km, and the capital at 24 km. The five short-named ad sets ran one day (5 May 2025) after a rename and are outside the final quota groups, so their people never qualify. No screening question beyond consent; a phone number is asked early and again at the end.

who_qualified: adults who had not completed a university degree and chose English; reached the end of the questions, about 13 minutes in
qualify_rule: answered the mobile-operator question at the end, and chose English or Swahili (as the quota rule was written)
notes: The final quota rule asks for language = English or 'Swahili', but the answer was stored as 'Kiswahili', so only people who chose English qualify under the rule as written (kept as written; hence the language:en tag). Each gender had two ad sets (by language) that people's labels do not separate; pooled. Screen-outs: under 18, a university or higher degree, an age answer that contradicts the age band.

qualify_rule: answered the last question of the first questionnaire
notes: Whole country, men and women. The ad message said 'up to 225 KES' (to 150 on 12 Dec), across two questionnaires; the consent text says 75 KES per questionnaire. Two attention checks screen out.
